memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Go, consecrate the people. Tell them, 'Consecrate yourselves in preparation for tomorrow; for this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: There are devoted things among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them. In the morning, present yourselves tribe by tribe. The tribe the Lord chooses shall come forward clan by clan; the clan the Lord chooses shall come forward family by family; and the family the Lord chooses shall come forward man by man. Whoever is caught with the devoted things shall be destroyed by fire, along with all that belongs to him. He has violated the covenant of the Lord and has done an outrageous thing in Israel!'" — Josh 7:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God lays out a careful process for uncovering the sin. The people are to consecrate themselves, then present themselves the next day, and God Himself will single out the guilty one — tribe by tribe, clan by clan, family by family, man by man. What patience and precision. God narrows it down step by step, giving space at every stage.

Notice first the call to "consecrate yourselves." Before dealing with sin, the people must set themselves apart for God, preparing their hearts. Addressing sin is holy work, and it begins with a right posture before the Lord. We cannot casually stroll into repentance; we come reverently, taking God's holiness seriously.

Notice too the plain diagnosis: "You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them." As long as the sin remained, Israel would keep failing. Some victories are impossible until we deal honestly with what is wrong inside us. God will not simply paper over sin; it must be brought out and removed.

This slow, deliberate process also reveals God's mercy. He does not strike the whole nation. He carefully isolates the guilty, and along the way He gives Achan opportunity after opportunity to step forward and confess. Even in judgment, God leaves room for repentance. That same patient mercy meets us in the gospel. God searches us out, not to destroy us, but to bring our sin into the light where it can be dealt with through the cleansing found in Christ (Ps 139:23-24).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the "holy work" of repentance seriously, preparing your heart before God?
2. Is there a victory you long for that requires first dealing with something inside you?
3. How does God's step-by-step patience with Achan reveal His mercy toward sinners?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me take repentance seriously and prepare my heart before You. Search me out, remove what hinders me, and cleanse me through Christ. Amen.
